subject: POC evaluation signals & ownership — Redwood x Archon
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Vohra <anya@archon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC evaluation signals & ownership — Redwood x Archon

Hi Anya — great conversation earlier. Quick post-call recap and proposed POC success signals so we have a single source of truth before we kick off. Attaching the sample prompts you shared and our lightweight runbook template.

Summary of objectives
- Validate integration with Archon ingestion + Redwood inference for the customer-facing assistant.
- Measure economics and latency at production-like load.
- Confirm quality on Archon intent extraction and hallucination tolerance.

Proposed success signals (please confirm):
1) Latency
   - P95 server-side inference latency <= 250 ms for responses up to ~512 tokens (measured at Redwood edge, post-auth).
2) Throughput
   - Sustained baseline of 40 requests/sec with 95% of requests under the latency target during the 2-hour load window.
3) Cost
   - Effective cost <= $0.60 per 1k tokens at the target throughput with our recommended batching.
4) Quality (Archon-defined)
   - Intent extraction F1 >= 0.92 on the curated 1,000-sample evaluation set.
   - Hallucination: named-entity mismatch rate < 1% on 200 negative-test prompts.
5) Availability
   - Service availability >= 99.9% during POC windows (monitoring and alerting integrated).

Operational ownership
- Jordan Blake: POC owner (commercial + timeline).
- Ben Carter: Ops lead (runbooks, canary rollout, telemetry).
- Karthik Iyer: Model/config lead (quantization, kernel selection, perf tuning).

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): NDA and sample workload + SOW sign-off.
- Week 1: Baseline integration + smoke validation (small sample).
- Week 2: Load window and initial tuning (2-day test, followed by tuning).
- Week 3: Final evaluation, cost readout, and decision meeting.

Immediate next steps
- Anya: confirm the measurement windows and that the attached prompt set is representative.
- Archon procurement: if you can loop in procurement contact for SOW/Docusign, we’ll send a short SOW (1 page).
- Ben/Karthik: we’ll draft the runbook and canary plan once Anya confirms traffic shape.

Attachments: archon_sample_prompts.csv, redwood-poc-template.xlsx

Thanks — sending this as the working doc. If these signals look good I’ll lock them and kick off the SOW flow.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwood.ai)

From: Anya Vohra <anya@archon.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@archon.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC evaluation signals & ownership — Redwood x Archon

Thanks Jordan — that aligns well with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side:
1) Throughput: our peak expected ingress during real-user hours is closer to ~60 req/sec (short bursts to 100 rps). Can you confirm whether the latency target is achievable at burst conditions or if we should define separate steady-state vs burst buckets? Attached a short traffic profile.
2) Quality: the 1k eval set is fine; we also want to reserve an additional 200 "edge cases" for hallucination checks (we called these out in the doc).

Procurement (procurement@archon.ai) — looping you in for SOW logistics. We prefer a two-week trial with the option to extend based on evaluation.

I’m fine with the ownership breakdown. Once you confirm the throughput approach and send the SOW I’ll get procurement to review.

Best,
Anya
CTO, Archon.ai
(anya@archon.ai)

Attachment: archon-expected-traffic.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 16:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC evaluation signals & ownership — Redwood x Archon

Jordan / Karthik — quick ops readout and what I can deliver this week:
- I reviewed the attached traffic profile. We should treat 60 rps as the baseline for the POC and plan for 100 rps bursts. We’ll run a 2-hour steady-state window at 60 rps and two 30-minute burst windows at up to 100 rps.
- Canary rollout: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% across the test window; each step gated by error rate and P95 latency.
- Cost sensitivity: tokenization differences between Archon text and our tokenizer may change the effective tokens-per-response by ~10-18%. I’ll include a tokenization delta in the cost readout.
- Model config: propose we test two quantization/latency profiles:
   a) q4_0 (higher quality, higher cost)
   b) q8_0 (lower cost, slightly higher latency variance)

I attached a short ops runbook draft (ops-runbook-v1.md) that documents telemetry events we’ll collect (inference_latency_ms, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, token_count, error_code).

I’ll stand up the test infra and a Grafana dashboard; need sample API keys and the annotated 1k eval set from Archon.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Vohra <anya@archon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@archon.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 18:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC evaluation signals & ownership — Redwood x Archon

Perfect — thanks for the rapid confirmation, Anya, and great ops plan Ben. I’ll adjust the success signals to define steady-state vs burst buckets as you suggested:
- Steady-state: 60 rps window, P95 <= 250 ms.
- Burst: 100 rps short windows, P95 <= 400 ms (tolerance for tail during bursts).

Updated timeline: we’ll start week-of July 6 so Archon has time to hand over API keys and the annotated eval sets. I’ve uploaded the one-page SOW and a Google Drive folder with the runbook drafts here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcdEFgHIjK-lAbc123. DocuSign SOW link: https://www.docusign.com/summary/ABC-POC-SOW-789.

Once procurement confirms the SOW we’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff (Ben/Karthik + Archon engs) to agree on telemetry and test windows.

Thanks — locking owners and next steps.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwood.ai)
